Exploratory data analysis: test group differences of several variables

Source: R/eda_interactive.R
eda_test.Rd

Tests for each variable whether it differs between the groups (e.g. the clusters of a segmentation): an omnibus test of all groups and, for numeric variables, comparisons of each group with the total (default), the rest of the sample, the mean of the group means, or all other groups.

Usage

eda_test(
  data,
  vars,
  group,
  weight = NULL,
  treat_as = c("auto", "numeric", "categorical"),
  method = c("parametric", "nonparametric"),
  reference = c("total", "rest", "meandev", "groups"),
  p_adjust = "holm",
  min_labels = 5
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, typically a haven-labelled tibble, or the output of seg_cluster() (see "Grouping by a cluster solution").

vars

The variables to describe: a character vector of names or a tidyselect expression, e.g. dplyr::starts_with("F50_0_").

group

Name of the grouping variable (e.g. "cluster_k4").

weight

Optional. Name of a weight variable.

treat_as

"auto" (default), "numeric" or "categorical". See "Numeric or categorical?".

method

"parametric" (default) or "nonparametric". See "Statistical tests".

reference

"total" (default), "rest", "meandev" or "groups". See "Statistical tests".

p_adjust

Method to adjust the p-values of the comparisons (see stats::p.adjust()). Defaults to "holm".

min_labels

Minimum number of value labels or distinct values for a variable to be treated as numeric (with treat_as = "auto"). Defaults to 5.

Value

An object of class eda_test, a list with the elements:

  • omnibus: tibble with one row per variable: test, statistic (F, Kruskal-Wallis H or chi-square), df1, df2, p, effect (name of the effect size), effect_size, effect_ci_low, effect_ci_high, n.

  • pairwise: tibble with the comparisons of the numeric variables: group1, group2 (the other group, or "Total", "Rest", "Mean of groups"), estimate1, estimate2 (means, or medians if nonparametric), difference, direction, se, ci_low, ci_high (of the difference), t, df, p, p_adj.

  • settings: list of the settings used.

Details

Numeric and categorical variables are distinguished as in eda_describe().

Statistical tests

Numeric variables: omnibus test

Does the variable differ between any of the groups?

  • method = "parametric" (default): one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA, F-test of the linear model variable ~ group; weighted least squares if weight is given). Effect size: eta squared (effectsize::eta_squared()), the share of the variance explained by the groups, with confidence interval.

  • method = "nonparametric": Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test (stats::kruskal.test()), which compares the distributions of the ranks instead of the means and is robust to outliers and skewed or ordinal data. Effect size: rank epsilon squared (effectsize::rank_epsilon_squared()). Weights are ignored.

Numeric variables: comparisons

Which groups differ from the reference? All comparisons are linear contrasts of the group means of one linear model variable ~ group, estimated with modelbased::estimate_contrasts():

  • The standard errors are heteroscedasticity-consistent (vcov = "HC3"), so the groups may have different variances (as in Welch's t-test).

  • Each contrast is tested with a t-test (degrees of freedom: residual degrees of freedom of the model).

  • If weight is given, the model is fitted with weighted least squares, so the group means and the total are weighted.

  • The p-values are adjusted for the number of comparisons within each variable (p_adjust, default Holm), reported as p_adj.

The reference (reference) defines the contrasts:

  • "total" (default): each group vs. the total including the group, i.e. the (weighted) mean of all respondents, as shown by the "Total" bar of eda_plot(). The contrast is \(\bar{y}_g - \sum_k p_k \bar{y}_k\), with \(p_k\) the (weighted) share of group \(k\). Its standard error accounts for the group being part of the total; a simple two-sample test of the group against the total would wrongly treat them as independent samples.

  • "rest": each group vs. the rest of the sample (all respondents not in the group). As \(\bar{y}_g - \bar{y}_{total} = (1 - p_g)(\bar{y}_g - \bar{y}_{rest})\), this test has exactly the same t- and p-values as "total"; only the reported difference is larger.

  • "meandev": each group vs. the unweighted mean of the group means (deviation or "effect" coding, comparison = "meandev" in modelbased::estimate_contrasts()). Every group counts equally, regardless of its size. This equals "total" only if all groups are of the same size.

  • "groups": all pairs of groups (comparison = "pairwise").

With method = "nonparametric", the same contrasts are computed on the ranks of the variable (rank-transformation approach of Conover & Iman, 1981), i.e. the groups are compared by their mean ranks; weights are ignored. The estimates are then reported as medians, and the standard errors and confidence intervals (on the rank scale) are omitted.

direction tells whether the group (group1) is "higher" or "lower" than the reference (by the contrast of the means or of the mean ranks).

Categorical variables

Pearson's chi-square test of independence of the variable and the groups (stats::chisq.test(), without continuity correction). Effect size: Cramér's V (effectsize::cramers_v(), not bias-corrected). If weighted, the weighted contingency table is rescaled to the unweighted sample size before testing, so that the weights do not inflate the sample size. There are no comparisons of single groups for categorical variables.

Limitations

The weighted tests treat the weights as precision weights of a linear model. This is an approximation; for design-based inference (strata, clusters, calibration weights), use the survey package. Many tests (many variables and groups) increase the chance of false positives; the p-values are only adjusted within each variable, not across variables.

For a detailed plot of a single variable with further tests (e.g. robust or Bayesian), see eda_plot_detail().

References

Conover, W. J., & Iman, R. L. (1981). Rank transformations as a bridge between parametric and nonparametric statistics. The American Statistician, 35(3), 124-129.

See also

Other eda: eda_describe(), eda_explore(), eda_plot(), eda_plot_detail()

Examples

eda_test(
  sm_synthetic,
  vars = c("F50_0_1", "F50_0_2", "gender"),
  group = "cluster_benchmark",
  weight = "weight"
)
